build.instructions:
App name for the person: Job Opening Tracker

What success looks like: The user can add an opening in a few seconds, log each step they take on it, and see at a glance which openings are at which stage and what still needs action.

How the person will use it:
- Add an opening with company, role, where it was found, a pasted link and notes. -> It is saved with today's date and the stage 'Found', and appears at the top of the list.
- Open an opening and log a step, such as 'Applied' or 'Emailed recruiter', with a date and short note. -> The step is added to that opening's history and its stage updates to match.
- Change an opening's stage directly, for example to 'Rejected'. -> The list shows the new stage and the change is recorded as a dated step.
- Filter the list by stage, for example everything applied to but not yet answered. -> Only matching openings are shown, newest activity first, with a count per stage.

What it keeps:
- collection Job openings: Hold each opening the user wants to keep track of.. Fields: Company (text, required), Role (text, required), Where I found it (text), Link (text), Stage (choice, required), Date found (date, required), Notes (text)
- collection Steps taken: Record each thing the user did about an opening, in order.. Fields: Opening (reference, required), Date (date, required), What I did (choice, required), Note (text)

What it does:
- action add_opening: Saves a new opening with company, role and optional source, link and notes. Sets today's date and the stage 'Found'. Refuses to save if company or role is empty. (inputs: company, role, where I found it, link, notes; outputs: the saved opening)
- action log_step: Adds a dated step to an opening's history and moves the opening's stage to match the step when it clearly implies one (for example 'Applied' sets the stage to Applied). (inputs: opening, date, what I did, note; outputs: the saved step, updated stage)
- action set_stage: Sets the stage of an opening directly and records the date of the change as a step. (inputs: opening, new stage; outputs: updated opening)
- action review_list: Shows openings filtered by stage, ordered by most recent activity, with a count of openings in each stage. (inputs: stage filter; outputs: filtered list, counts per stage)

Constraints:
- Everything is stored only on this Mac and visible only to the user.
- Links are stored as text; no listing content is fetched.
- No messages, emails or reminders are sent.

Agreed assumptions:
- Resolved: each opening keeps a running log of every dated step, with the stage updating to match.
- Resolved: the add form captures company, role, where I found it, link and notes; location, pay range and deadline are left out of version one.
- Default stages: Found, Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Rejected, Withdrew - editable later.
- Default list order: most recent activity first, with quick filters and a count per stage.
- Links are stored as plain text; nothing is fetched from the web, and no reminders are sent.
- Everything stays on this Mac until you delete it; follow-up dates and stats over time can be added later.

Built the package. Summary of what's in it:

**`package/app.yaml`** — collections `job_openings` (company, role, where_i_found_it, link, stage, date_found, notes, last_activity) and `steps_taken` (opening, date, what_i_did, note); views `job_openings.list` (filterable by stage, newest activity first) and `steps_taken.for_opening`.

**`package/src/app_code/handlers.py`** — `add_opening` (refuses empty company or role, sets today's date and stage `Found`), `log_step` (stores the dated step and moves the stage when the step implies one), `set_stage` (sets the stage and records it as a dated step), `review_list` (stage-filtered openings, newest activity first, plus a count per stage). Compiles cleanly with the platform interpreter.

**`package/ui/src/main.tsx`** — one screen: an "Add an opening" Form with Company, Role, Where I found it, Link, Notes and an "Add opening" button; the openings table (Company, Role, Stage, Where I found it, Date found) with per-stage filter buttons showing counts; opening a row reveals a drawer to log a step (Date, What I did, Note → "Log step"), change the stage ("Change stage") and read that opening's history.

Two things to note: I could not inspect the installed `alpha_sdk` or `@alpha/ui-kit` type definitions (they live outside the working directory and the sandbox denied both the directory listing and an arbitrary `python -c` run), so the handlers stick strictly to the documented SDK surface and raise plain `ValueError` for refusals, and the screen uses only documented kit props — `SelectField`'s `options` shape is my one inference. I also could not machine-validate `app.yaml`, so it is hand-checked against the contract.

The app declares the actions `add_opening`, `log_step`, `set_stage` and `review_list` behind a single "Job Opening Tracker" screen at `ui/src/main.tsx`.
